newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian activists sentenced for subversion.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian activists sentenced for subversion.

text.p: Two Indonesian activists from the unrecognised People's Democratic Party (PRD), the last of a batch of 14 arrested last year after riots in Jakarta, were convicted of subversion on Monday and sentenced to jail.

The south Jakarta district court sentenced I Gusti Agung Anom Astika to four years imprisonment and Wilson Bin Nurtias to five years in separate trials for undermining the state ideology of Pancasila.
"The defendant has discredited the New Order," said judge I.B.W. Somya when sentencing Astika.
The New Order is the term used to describe President Suharto's government since he took power in the mid 1960s. Subversion carries a maximum penalty of death in Indonesia.
In April, 12 PRD members were given jail terms of between 18 months and 13 years in Jakarta and the city of Surabaya after being convicted of subversion.
All 14 were arrested after riots in Jakarta on July 27 last year, the worst violence in the city for over two decades.

The riots erupted after police and a government-backed faction of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) raided the party's headquarters and evicted supporters of its ousted chief Megawati Sukarnoputri.

The military has also blamed the PRD as well as other unnamed "third parties" for sparking widespread rioting, mostly on the main island of Java, during the 27-day campaign ahead of last month's general elections.
